sources.entry: Mathematics for the adventurous self-learner, Neil Sainsbury

summary.title: Mathematics for the adventurous self-learner
summary.one_liner: A six-year self-study guide to undergraduate mathematics, with a curated book and course path from foundations through analysis, algebra, and topology, plus advice on exercises and avoiding burnout.
keywords: how to avoid burnout learning math
coding the matrix linear algebra python
takeaways: Choose self-study books that include exercises and solutions, and prefer print over Kindle for math texts.
Follow a suggested order of books from foundations (Art of Problem Solving, Savov) through proofs, calculus, analysis, linear algebra, algebra and topology.
Do not insist on solving every exercise; look up solutions after a reasonable time (around 20 minutes minimum) to avoid burnout.
Dover books are a low-cost option; MIT OpenCourseWare offers free courses with lectures, problems and exams.
summary.summary: The author, a software developer, describes six years of self-studying undergraduate mathematics and shares an annotated reading list organised by topic: foundations, history, proofs, calculus and analysis, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, differential equations, algebra, topology and number theory. Each recommendation includes notes on difficulty, exercises, solutions availability and how it compares with alternatives. The page also gives practical advice on choosing books, using MIT OpenCourseWare and Dover editions, and pacing exercises to sustain motivation. The text is cut off partway through the number theory section.
